//: The stack registry, as a table.
A stack is a curated combination of capability tags and verticals
that produces a coherent greenfield project: pick one with
`keel new --stack=<id>` and the engine resolves everything from
there. Stacks are sugar — they add no expressive power the
composition layer does not already have — and nothing in one is
code, which is why they live here rather than in stacks.ts.
No preset is written out here: each is a cell of this table. A
`platforms` row is a language on a runtime and framework — the
tags and build systems its cells share — and its `cells` are the
entrypoint sets it offers, each keyed by its words joined by `+`
in `entrypoints` order (`cli`, `http`, `cli+http`, `spa`) and
valued by the one sentence `keel new --list` describes it with.
The rest is the table's: `entrypoints` gives each word its tag and
the `projects` it puts in a product's scope, and `singles` the
tags, module layouts and verticals every cell carries, in install
order (`vcs` first, so the project is a repo before files land) —
`{ "id": …, "with": "http" }` only in a cell with that entrypoint.
A row's `buildSystems` and the module layouts are the dials a cell
offers, the first the default; a row declaring `buildSystems` omits
the `pkg.*` tag from `tags`, and every cell the `layout.*` one, for
the install handler folds the chosen option's tag in. A cell's id
is its row's `id` with `{entrypoints}` spelled out word by word, in
the row's `words` where it has its own (the JVM rows say `rest`
where the others say `http`). A set no row lists is no preset, and
`keel new` refuses it.
A product is one stack per service: a `products` rule crosses its
services' `stacks`, one product per combination, first service
outermost. In its `id` and `description`, `{<path>}` is the stack
at that path, and the `id` then drops each word in `unsaid` — what
every product of the rule says already (its backend serves HTTP,
and Quarkus, keel's default, goes unnamed): `quarkus-rest` makes
`fullstack`, and `go-cli-http`, were it listed, would make
`fullstack-go-cli`. A service's stack is a cell of this table,
never a product: products do not nest.
An id is permanent: a product root records its services' ids on
disk, so no edit here may rename a cell.
`tests/domain/core/stack-registry.test.ts` holds what this table
generates to its golden, field for field, and fails until the
golden is edited to match.
`src/domain/core/stack-table.ts` validates this file against
`StackTableSchema` and expands it into the preset document
`stacks.ts` resolves — the `StackPresetsSchema` a preset from
outside this repository satisfies. It expands in the registry's
order: a platform's languages together (rows whose tags other than
`lang.*` are the same set), its one-entrypoint cells before its
composed ones, then the products, rule by rule. The registry golden
pins that order, and converge reads it: where two products have a
service on one preset, the first registered is the one converge
takes that service's given verticals and scope from (`givenOf`,
`serviceGiving` in `converge.ts`). Every menu sorts by id.
Adding a platform is a row, and an entrypoint set a cell; adding a
product is its backend's id in the `stacks` of the rule's `backend`
service. The product glue gives that backend its image and its run
hint by family, read off its tags (`adapters/product-families.ts`),
so a backend tagged like a family keel builds needs no glue edit.
Either reaches every menu and the finder by itself.
